condition: Cervical screening overdue — HPV-based primary screening
permutationLabel: Woman aged 34, last cytology 6 years ago
summary: 34-year-old woman at a wellness visit, last cervical cytology 6 years ago (normal). WHO 2021: HPV DNA primary screening from 30, every 5–10 years; USPSTF 2018: at 30–65 hrHPV every 5 years, co-testing every 5 or cytology every 3.

inputs.hpi: Well 34-year-old at a wellness visit. Last cervical smear 6 years ago in Martinique, reported normal; none since. No intermenstrual or post-coital bleeding, no discharge. HIV test 2 years ago negative. Copper IUD for contraception.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Cervical screening overdue — age 34
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic. Cervical screening overdue (last 6 years ago). Primary HPV test (self- or clinician-collected); if not available, cytology.

mustInclude.note: From 30, HPV testing is the preferred primary screen (WHO 2021) or one of three options (USPSTF 2018).

mustNotAlarm.note: An asymptomatic screening visit must not raise an "emergency now" banner (alarm fatigue; front desk would redirect a well person).

guideline.name: WHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions (2nd edition)
guideline.section: General population: HPV DNA detection as the primary screening test, starting at 30 years, every 5–10 years; women living with HIV from 25 years, every 3–5 years
guideline.citation: World Health Organization. WHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions for cervical cancer prevention, 2nd ed. Geneva: WHO; 2021.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for cervical cancer
guideline.section: 21–29: cytology every 3 years; 30–65: cytology every 3 years, high-risk HPV testing alone every 5 years, or co-testing every 5 years (grade A); recommend against screening after hysterectomy with removal of the cervix and no history of CIN 2+ or cancer (grade D)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for cervical cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2018;320:674–686.

rationale: Cervical screening at 30 and over is HPV-based in current WHO and USPSTF guidance. A fixed "smear every 3 years" prompt is out of date for this age group.

authoring.author: Claude (prevention/screening, obstetric-gynaecological mimics and paediatric surgery cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Every citation is verified: false. iOS outcomes are unverified (not run on Linux); triage after the first CI run.
